correctness.rationale: For a state permutation p, A′(x)=−Σ_j M_{p(j),j}≤C=−Σ_j min_i M_{ij} and ≤R=−Σ_i min_j M_{ij}. With C≤R, equality to min{C,R} holds iff all chosen values are column minima, yielding a perfect matching in BC(M); the row case is symmetric, with C=R handled. A matching is unique iff there is no matching-alternating cycle because toggling a cycle yields another and the symmetric difference of two distinct matchings decomposes into alternating cycles. Directed cycle detection after finding one matching gives a polynomial algorithm. Independently enumerated ALL binary matrices of sizes n=1,2,3,4 (2,16,512,65536 matrices); direct grid-state permutation counts matched graph minimizer matchings at every case, including 4160 no-state matrices at n=4, 15432 unique and 45944 multiple. This finite test corroborates, but is not the universal proof.
